title: A player found a visibility problem I missed in my AI-assisted sorting game
author: TidyShuffle
selftext:
A player tried Tidy Shuffle and told me some of the objects blend into the rugs. They also said the glow that kicks in when they're stuck helped. I had spent a lot of time checking which box an object belongs in. I hadn't noticed how hard some objects were to see against the room itself.



It's my first Android game. I used Claude Code for Unity work and solution replay tests, Codex for visual review, and AI tools for art and audio. The replay tests still matter because the small tray makes it easy to accidentally make a level unsolvable. The feedback made me want to test something different too: take one room where this happens, look at the changed objects on a phone against the actual rug, and see whether the glow helps without giving away the next move.



For anyone who uses generated art in a puzzle game, how do you catch low contrast once the assets are in the level? I'm especially curious what you check on a real device. Tidy Shuffle is free on Android with ads and an optional purchase.
